text: {"findings": [{"start_s": 3.0, "end_s": 5.0, "pattern": "Broken cause and effect", "evidence": "At t=4 the tower is already leaning right while the ball is around x≈330, roughly 80 px short of the tower base at x≈430, so the tower starts falling before any contact.", "impact": "The video is meant to show the hit causing the fall, but the frames show the collapse starting on its own.", "confidence": "high", "basis": "frame inspection", "fix": "Delay the tower's topple until the frame where the ball actually touches the bottom block."}, {"start_s": 4.0, "end_s": 5.0, "pattern": "Implausible physics", "evidence": "The bottom block, which was resting at x≈430–480, slides to x≈490–540 and the tower topples to the right, while the ball is still left of the tower or only just reaching it.", "impact": "A base sliding away from a ball that has not pushed it reads as unmotivated, unnatural motion.", "confidence": "medium", "basis": "frame inspection", "fix": "Keep the base block anchored until impact and drive the topple from the ball's momentum at the contact point."}, {"start_s": 5.0, "end_s": 8.0, "pattern": "Implausible physics", "evidence": "The fallen blocks extend from about y≈282 to y≈325, below the ground surface at y≈316, so they appear sunk into the floor in every remaining frame.", "impact": "Objects passing into the ground breaks the solidity of the scene.", "confidence": "medium", "basis": "frame inspection", "fix": "Correct the collision bounds so the fallen blocks rest on top of the ground line."}]}
